summary: Ofer from Vectara explains that building an enterprise-scale RAG stack is far harder than most realize. He begins with a RAG architecture overview: an ingestion flow where data from documents, databases, or SaaS tools is parsed, chunked, embedded, and stored in a vector database; and a query flow where a question is embedded, relevant facts are retrieved (potentially via hybrid search and reranking), sent with a prompt to an LLM, and optionally checked for hallucinations. Vectara packages this entire stack as a service—handling extraction, encoding, indexing, vector database, and retrieval—available as SaaS, in-VPC, or on-premise, exposing only indexing and querying APIs. The core of the talk identifies seven pitfalls of DIY RAG. First, hallucinations and response quality require significant investment in parsing, chunking, hybrid search, evaluation, and explainability with provenance tracking. Second, latency compounds across multiple components, with the weakest link determining overall speed. Third, scaling introduces GPU, CPU, storage, and token costs that escalate rapidly at production scale. Fourth, security demands attribute-based access control and proper handling of sensitive data like PHI and PII. Fifth, vendor chaos arises when multiple components come from different vendors, complicating contracts, integration, diagnostics, and support. Sixth, maintaining the stack requires scarce, specialized expertise across LLMs, embeddings, search, data engineering, DevOps, and security. Seventh, multi-language support is difficult because not all components support non-English languages. Ofer then details why enterprises choose Vectara: accuracy through built-in hallucination detection and retrieval quality, security via access controls and prompt attack prevention, and observability with citations throughout the flow. Vectara's Hallucination Evaluation Model (HHM) is integrated into every call, returning a hallucination score. The model was open-sourced on Hugging Face with over 3 million downloads, making it the most popular hallucination evaluation available. Vectara also maintains a leaderboard evaluating LLMs' hallucination tendencies, revealing that some models hallucinate at rates of 10–14%, underscoring the importance of careful model selection. A 30-day free trial with full platform capabilities is available.

takeaways: Building an enterprise-scale RAG stack is significantly harder than initial prototypes suggest, with at least seven major hidden pitfalls.
RAG architecture involves complex ingestion (parsing, chunking, embedding, vector storage) and query flows (retrieval, hybrid search, reranking, LLM generation, hallucination detection).

Hallucination prevention requires continuous investment; Vectara's built-in HHM model (open-sourced, 3M+ downloads) returns a hallucination score with every query, and a leaderboard shows some LLMs hallucinate at 10–14% rates.
Latency, cost, and scaling challenges compound across multiple stack components, with token and infrastructure costs escalating at production volume.
Security requires attribute-based access control, prompt attack prevention, and proper handling of sensitive data like PHI and PII throughout the entire RAG pipeline.
Vendor chaos from using multiple component vendors creates integration complexity and diagnostic finger-pointing problems.
Maintaining a DIY RAG stack demands scarce, cross-functional expertise in LLMs, embeddings, search, data engineering, DevOps, and security.
Turnkey RAG-as-a-service platforms like Vectara handle all stack components via simple APIs, offering accuracy, security, observability, and deployment flexibility (SaaS, in-VPC, on-premise).

sections.title: Introduction and RAG Architecture Overview
sections.summary: Ofer introduces himself and explains RAG: instead of calling an LLM directly, you retrieve relevant facts from your data and ground the LLM response in them. He outlines the two main flows: ingestion (extracting, chunking, embedding, storing in vector database) and query (embedding the query, vector search, optional hybrid search and reranking, sending facts to LLM, optional hallucination detection). He introduces Vectara as a RAG-as-a-service platform that packages all components, available as SaaS, in-VPC, or on-premise.

sections.title: Seven Pitfalls of DIY RAG - Part 1
sections.summary: Ofer covers the first four pitfalls. (1) Hallucinations and quality require investment in parsing, chunking, hybrid search, continuous evaluation, and explainability with provenance. (2) Latency compounds across components with the weakest link setting overall speed. (3) Scaling introduces GPU, CPU, storage, and token costs that escalate from 10 documents to millions. (4) Security demands attribute-based access control and proper handling of sensitive data like PHI and PII.

sections.title: Seven Pitfalls of DIY RAG - Part 2
sections.summary: Ofer covers the remaining three pitfalls. (5) Vendor chaos arises from multiple component vendors creating contract complexity, integration costs, and diagnostic finger-pointing. (6) Unsustainable maintenance requires scarce expertise across LLMs, embeddings, search, data engineering, DevOps, and security. (7) Multi-language support is difficult because not all components support non-English languages, degrading quality. He concludes that these pitfalls motivate Vectara's plug-and-play RAG-as-a-service platform.

sections.title: Vectara's Solution, Hallucination Detection, and Conclusion
sections.summary: Ofer details Vectara's turnkey approach: extraction, encoding, indexing, vector database, and retrieval are all managed by the platform, with users accessing only indexing and querying APIs. Three main reasons enterprises choose Vectara: accuracy (hallucination reduction, retrieval quality), security (access controls, prompt attack prevention), and observability with citations. He highlights Vectara's Hallucination Evaluation Model (HHM), integrated into every query call to return a hallucination score. The model was open-sourced on Hugging Face with over 3 million downloads, making it the most popular hallucination evaluation available. Vectara maintains a leaderboard showing LLM hallucination rates, with some models reaching 10–14%. Deployment options include SaaS, in-VPC, and on-premise. He invites attendees to try a 30-day free trial.
